reason: A frame and mesh seem suited to making a surface that spreads the rover's weight across the drift.
expectation: I expect to make some kind of traction or load-spreading track, though I don't know its exact form.

alternatives.reason: Sifting gravel might also help build a crossing, but the mesh and frame seem more directly like tracks.

effect: The panels match my expectation and seem ready for the crossing; I still need to prepare the gravel.
reaction: Satisfying to see the frame and mesh become traction panels.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and sieving the firm patch may supply material for the crossing.
expectation: I expect a graded gravel supply, though I am unsure how it will be used with the panels.

effect: The sieve produced coarse gravel, which can now be combined with the panels.
reaction: That makes the next step clear, though I am curious how gravel and panels work together.
reason: This is the only combination and joins the two crossing materials.
expectation: I expect gravel-filled or gravel-backed traction panels for the soft drift.

effect: The gravel-filled tracks complete the crossing preparation; the chapter ends before the crossing itself.
reaction: The finished tracks are satisfying, though I wanted to see them used on the drift.

mostWorthwhile.text: Combining the gravel and panels made a concrete solution to spreading the rover's load; I could picture the finished tracks.

leastWorthwhile.text: Sieving the gravel was a rather plain intermediate action, with no detail beyond its name.

surprise.text: I was mildly surprised that the chapter ended with the tracks prepared, before using them to reach the seam.

arbitrary.text: The gravel's role was initially unclear: I could guess it would help the crossing, but didn't know it would fill the panels until the combination.

continue.text: Yes. I want to cross the drift and find out whether the intact ice contains another ridged fragment; the short preparation left that question open.
